rationale: Submits a probe built from a distinction the earlier stall attempt missed: registering a VerifyLeader request needs the leader's main loop, but counting the acknowledgement it waits for does not, because those votes arrive on replication goroutines. Each trial therefore lets the leader register the request first, isolates it from every peer so it has no second acknowledgement, then stalls its main loop inside StoreLogs and only afterwards reconnects the non-voter, at a delay chosen to fall after a voter majority has elected a successor. If the acknowledgement is counted while the loop is blocked, the request returns success even though a successor already leads at a higher term. The discriminating fields are the verify endpoint, the sample at which another server was first seen in Leader state and whether that preceded the verdict. Its execution is requested under the verify question, whose open gap asks exactly which legal condition permits this; no observation is claimed until the receipt exists.

scope.description: Six trials that each build a three-voter plus one-non-voter cluster, register a VerifyLeader request at the leader while it is isolated from every peer, stall its main loop inside StoreLogs for 900ms, then reconnect only the non-voter after 250 to 500ms and record the verify endpoint, when a different server was first sampled in Leader state, whether that preceded the verdict, the terms involved and the stall counters.
assumptions: The stalling log store models a leader whose disk stall blocks its own main loop; it is a supplied dependency, not a change to production logic.
Reconnecting the non-voter is a legal topology change: the transport is simply reconnected to a server that remains in the leader's latest configuration as a non-voter.

HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms and a 900ms stall mean the leader's lease case cannot run during the stall while a voter majority can campaign at 200ms and elect a successor.
In-memory transports in one process, so RPC round trips are far faster than in a networked cluster.
excluded: Multi-host clocks and process-level suspensions; and any case where the leader's own term is raised, since the partition keeps it at its old term.

experiment.prefix: Each trial builds four real Raft instances in one process with their own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, fully connected before any node starts; the three voters get a log store whose StoreLogs sleeps 900ms while armed, and only the elected leader's store is armed. The three voters are bootstrapped as Voter and the fourth node joins through the leader's AddNonvoter call. The trial emits assurance_registered_setup, disconnects the leader from both other voters and from the non-voter, calls VerifyLeader on the leader, waits 30ms so the main loop registers the request, arms the stall and drives one Apply so the leader's main loop blocks inside StoreLogs, starts a 1ms sampler over all four servers, then after the configured delay reconnects only the leader and the non-voter and waits for the verify future. It emits assurance_registered_result with the endpoint, the verdict time, whether another server was sampled in Leader state and when, the maximum term seen, the leader's term and state, and the stall counters. The harness is TestAssuranceVerifyRegisteredThenStalled.

comparisons.description: The stalled leader returned VerifyLeader success even though it could reach no voter for the whole window.
A successor was sampled in Leader state before the verify returned, so the verdict and the successor overlapped.
Conditional on a successor preceding the verdict: whether the leader still reported success. Holds means the stale-read verdict was witnessed.
